module

public import Mathlib.Data.ENat.Lattice
public import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
public import Mathlib.Order.CompletePartialOrder
import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum.Ineq

@[expose] public section

def Triplewise {α : Type*} (r : α → α → α → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃i j k ⦄, i ≠ j → j ≠ k → i ≠ k → r i j k

namespace Set

variable {α : Type*} {r : α → α → α → Prop} {s t : Set α} {x y z : α}

/--
The ternary relation `r` holds triplewise on the set `s`
if `r x y z` for all *distinct* `x y z ∈ s`.
-/
protected def Triplewise (s : Set α) (r : α → α → α → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → ∀ ⦃y⦄, y ∈ s → ∀ ⦃z⦄, z ∈ s → x ≠ y → y ≠ z → x ≠ z → r x y z

protected theorem Triplewise.eq (hs : s.Triplewise r)
    (hx : x ∈ s) (hy : y ∈ s) (hz : z ∈ s) (h : ¬r x y z) :
    x = y ∨ y = z ∨ x = z := by
  have := (h <| hs hx hy hz · · ·)
  tauto

theorem Triplewise.mono (h : t ⊆ s) (hs : s.Triplewise r) :
    t.Triplewise r :=
  fun _ hx _ hy _ hz hxy hyz hxz ↦ hs (h hx) (h hy) (h hz) hxy hyz hxz

@[simp]
theorem Triplewise_univ_iff :
    Set.univ.Triplewise r ↔ Triplewise r := by
  simp [Set.Triplewise, Triplewise]

theorem triplewise_of_encard_lt (r : α → α → α → Prop)
    (h : s.encard < 3) : s.Triplewise r := by
  unfold Set.Triplewise
  contrapose! h
  obtain ⟨x, hx, y, hy, z, hz, hxy, hyz, hxz, _⟩ := h
  trans encard {x, y, z}
  · simp [Set.encard_insert_of_notMem, *]
    norm_num
  · exact encard_le_encard_of_injOn (by simp [MapsTo, hx, hy, hz]) (injOn_id _)

@[simp]
theorem triplewise_empty (r : α → α → α → Prop) :
    Set.Triplewise ∅ r :=
  (notMem_empty · · |>.elim)

@[simp]
theorem triplewise_singleton (r : α → α → α → Prop) :
    Set.Triplewise {x} r := by
  apply triplewise_of_encard_lt
  simp

@[simp]
theorem triplewise_pair
    (r : α → α → α → Prop) : Set.Triplewise {x, y} r := by
  apply triplewise_of_encard_lt
  apply (encard_insert_le {y} x).trans_lt
  simp
  norm_num

theorem triplewise_insert :
    (insert x s).Triplewise r ↔ s.Triplewise r ∧
    ∀ y ∈ s, ∀ z ∈ s, x ≠ y → x ≠ z → y ≠ z → r x y z ∧ r y x z ∧ r y z x := by
  refine ⟨fun hxs ↦ ?_, fun ⟨hs, hxs⟩ ↦ ?_⟩
  · refine ⟨hxs.mono (subset_insert x s), fun y hy z hz hxy hxz hyz ↦ ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩⟩
    · exact hxs (mem_insert x s) (mem_insert_of_mem x hy) (mem_insert_of_mem x hz) hxy hyz hxz
    · exact hxs (mem_insert_of_mem x hy) (mem_insert x s) (mem_insert_of_mem x hz) hxy.symm hxz hyz
    · exact hxs (mem_insert_of_mem x hy) (mem_insert_of_mem x hz)
        (mem_insert x s) hyz hxz.symm hxy.symm
  · intro w hw y hy z hz hwy hyz hwz
    rw [mem_insert_iff] at hw hy hz
    obtain rfl | hw := hw
    · refine (hxs y ?_ z ?_ hwy hwz hyz).1
      · simpa [hwy.symm] using hy
      · simpa [hwz.symm] using hz
    obtain rfl | hy := hy
    · exact (hxs w hw z (by simpa [hyz.symm] using hz) hwy.symm hyz hwz).2.1
    obtain rfl | hz := hz
    · exact (hxs w hw y hy hwz.symm hyz.symm hwy).2.2
    exact hs hw hy hz hwy hyz hwz

theorem triplewise_insert_of_not_mem (hx : x ∉ s) :
    (insert x s).Triplewise r ↔ s.Triplewise r ∧
    ∀ y ∈ s, ∀ z ∈ s, y ≠ z → r x y z ∧ r y x z ∧ r y z x := by
  refine Set.triplewise_insert.trans <| and_congr_right' <| forall₄_congr ?_
  intro y hy z hz
  simp [(ne_of_mem_of_not_mem hy hx).symm, (ne_of_mem_of_not_mem hz hx).symm]

protected theorem Triplewise.insert (hs : s.Triplewise r)
    (h : ∀ y ∈ s, ∀ z ∈ s, x ≠ y → x ≠ z → y ≠ z → r x y z ∧ r y x z ∧ r y z x) :
    (insert x s).Triplewise r :=
  Set.triplewise_insert.mpr ⟨hs, h⟩

protected theorem Triplewise.insert_of_not_mem
    (hx : x ∉ s) (hs : s.Triplewise r)
    (h : ∀ y ∈ s, ∀ z ∈ s, y ≠ z → r x y z ∧ r y x z ∧ r y z x) :
    (insert x s).Triplewise r :=
  (Set.triplewise_insert_of_not_mem hx).mpr ⟨hs, h⟩

theorem triplewise_set_pred_iff {S : Set α} {P : Set α → Prop} :
    S.Triplewise (P {·, ·, ·}) ↔ ∀ T ⊆ S, T.ncard = 3 → P T := by
  constructor
  · intro h T hT T_ncard
    obtain ⟨x, y, z, hxy, hxz, hyz, rfl⟩ := ncard_eq_three.mp T_ncard
    simp_rw [insert_subset_iff, singleton_subset_iff] at hT
    exact h hT.1 hT.2.1 hT.2.2 hxy hyz hxz
  · intro h x hx y hy z hz hxy hyz hxz
    refine h _ ?_ (ncard_eq_three.mpr ⟨x, y, z, hxy, hxz, hyz, rfl⟩)
    simp [insert_subset_iff, hx, hy, hz]

end Set

reformulations.difference: The insertion criterion explicitly lists only three placements of the inserted element, rather than all six permutations of a distinct triple.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The remaining elements y and z are universally quantified in both orders. Applying the criterion to (y,z) gives r x y z, r y x z, and r y z x; applying it to (z,y) gives the other three permutations. No symmetry assumption on r is needed. An equivalence with the explicit six-permutation criterion was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: Three-element subsets are specified by T.ncard = 3 without a separate finiteness hypothesis.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Although ncard is zero on infinite sets, its positive value 3 forces finiteness. Thus T.ncard = 3 is equivalent to T.encard = 3 and selects exactly the ordinary three-element subsets, even when the ambient set is infinite. Both this cardinality equivalence and the theorem's encard-based formulation were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The source colors unordered three-element subsets; the Lean definition uses a predicate on ordered triples, two adjacent-transposition invariance conditions, and Set.Triplewise for homogeneity.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The two adjacent transpositions generate all permutations of three distinct elements. Consequently the predicate gives a well-defined color to each three-element subset, and its negation gives the other color. Conversely, any predicate on three-element subsets induces the required invariant ternary predicate. A full equivalence with the corresponding subset-coloring formulation, retaining the same red order type and blue cardinality, was proved in /workspace/review/use_sites.lean without sorry dependencies.

review.notes: Checked both definitions and all twelve lemmas. They consistently quantify over pairwise-distinct elements and agree with Mathlib's type/set Pairwise convention. Mathlib's List.Triplewise instead concerns increasing list positions; that is the expected container-specific distinction, not duplication or a conflicting set convention. Traced the Ramsey, union-free, non-collinearity, general-position, and isosceles uses against their sources. Both scratch files compile successfully; tests cover empty and small types/sets, repeated elements, infinite sets, asymmetric relations, and union-free boundary examples. Direct Erdős Problems requests were blocked by Cloudflare, so its content and exact LaTeX were read through r.jina.ai. No stale status was established: in particular, #130's page labels the combined chromatic/clique problem open, whereas the use site addresses only the chromatic-infinity subquestion; the page-level label alone does not establish a contradiction, and its linked external proof was not independently audited. The reviewed file remains byte-for-byte identical to the specified commit.
